Romania: 37.7% of adults obese. France: 12.5%. Same continent, a threefold gap. One map of European obesity, explained.

a thread 🧵🗺️

1/ The map shows the share of adults with a BMI over 30 in 2024. Romania 37.7%, Hungary 36.9%, Czechia 31.6%, Turkey 30.5%, UK 29.2%, Germany 24.5%. Data: WHO / NCD-RisC via Our World in Data (CC BY).
2/ The other end: France 12.5%, Switzerland 12.9%, Italy 17.9%, Sweden 18.7%, Spain 18.9%. The darkest purples cluster in Central and Eastern Europe.
3/ BMI is weight in kilograms divided by height in metres squared. The WHO calls 25 to 29.9 overweight and 30 or above obese.
4/ A caveat: BMI was designed for population statistics, not to judge one person. It can overstate body fat in muscular people and says nothing about where fat sits.
5/ That makes it useful for comparing countries, less so for individuals. Waist circumference or body fat percentage can say more about personal risk.
6/ The numbers are national averages, so they hide big differences within each country. Treat the map as a starting point, not a verdict.
Which of these surprised you most? Follow @forummapping for more maps like this.
